failedBlockers.reason: Requires architectural change to ASP.NET Core with Kestrel. .NET Framework Web Forms applications are fundamentally dependent on IIS system.webServer configuration including integrated pipeline handlers. Removing this section would break the application. This blocker can only be resolved through complete migration to ASP.NET Core, which is beyond minimal containerization fixes.

Requires architectural change to ASP.NET Core project format. The UseIISExpress and related settings are integral to .NET Framework Web Application project structure. These settings cannot be removed without converting the entire project to ASP.NET Core format (.csproj SDK-style project). This blocker requires full application migration, not a minimal fix.

notes: IMPORTANT: .NET Framework Web Forms applications require Windows containers with IIS. These fixes prepare the configuration for containerization but blocker-1 and blocker-2 indicate the application cannot run on Linux containers.

For Web.config environment variable substitution, use Web.config transformations (Web.Release.config) or replace #{VARIABLE}# tokens at deployment time using tools like tokenization in Azure DevOps or similar CI/CD pipelines.
The Health.aspx endpoint should be added to the project file and deployed. Access it at /Health.aspx for health checks.
Database migration required: Export data from LocalDB .mdf file and import to containerized SQL Server instance before deployment.
Persistent volumes must be configured in Docker/Kubernetes for: UPLOAD_PATH directory to retain uploaded tour images across container restarts.
